uncited: The method advects a quantity $\phi$ from time step $n$ to $n+1$ using two intermediate semi-Lagrangian advection operations.
*   **Time Complexity**: $O(N)$, where $N$ is the number of grid cells.
*   **Memory Complexity**: $O(N)$ for storing the field textures.
*   **Strengths**: Improved visual detail on low-resolution grids; reduces numerical smoothing (dissipation) compared to first-order semi-Lagrangian advection.

*   **Limitations**: Conditionally stable; requires careful tuning of the time step; more complex to implement than standard semi-Lagrangian advection; the limiter can introduce slight numerical diffusion if the range is tight.
The MacCormack scheme was originally developed for computational fluid dynamics and adapted for real-time GPU fluid simulation.
It is used in real-time 3D fluid solvers to advect velocity, density, and temperature fields.
